title: Latency normalizer and NetHealth prioritizer for region/tier routing
creator: Ava Mendez
description: Problem: Our current region selector uses raw p50 and p95 buckets and ad-hoc penalties for packet loss. This produces oscillation during noisy telemetry windows and does not compare fairly across POPs with different baseline latencies. Goal: replace ad-hoc heuristics with a normalized, explainable composite score that combines latency percentiles (p50/p95) and a network health index (packet loss, jitter, error-rate) to drive region selection and tier routing. The composite should support asymmetric penalties (prefer lower p95 penalties at higher SLO tiers), temporal decay to avoid rapid flips, and a fallback decision tree that selects compatible model variants (quantized, smaller sequence-length, or lower-beam variants) when no POP satisfies the composite threshold. Deliverables: scoring algorithm, rollout plan, telemetry/aggregator changes, new routing policy config schema, dashboards and alerts, canary traffic experiment and documentation for operators.
acceptance_criteria: Composite score computed per-POP every 10s: normalized p50 + normalized p95 + nethealth penalty -> single score in [0,100]
Normalization accounts for POP baseline: use rolling 7-day baseline median to z-normalize p50/p95 before fusion
NetHealth index combines packet loss, jitter, and TCP retransmit rate into a 0-100 penalty where 0 is healthy
Tier-aware weights: Dedicated (tier-1) multiplies p95 weight by 1.4, Hosted (tier-3) multiplies by 0.8
Temporal hysteresis: require 3 consecutive scoring windows (30s) before changing preferred POP unless score delta > 40
Fallback flow selects model variant with validated compatibility list and reduces routing score requirement by configurable delta
Integration tests: synthetic telemetry can trigger expected failover to fallback variant and to alternate POPs in stage environment
Observability: dashboard with per-POP composite score, contribution breakdown (p50/p95/nethealth), and alert when preferred POP changes > 5x/day
No user-visible latency regressions in canary (95th percentile change < 5% across canary traffic), and rollback plan documented

decisions: Use rolling 7-day POP baseline for normalization to avoid cross-POP bias
Composite score range standardized to 0-100 with configurable weights per tier
Hysteresis window set to 3 scoring windows (10s each) to reduce flapping; immediate override allowed for catastrophic nethealth values
Fallback selects smallest compatible model variant that preserves tokenization/response schema; operator opt-out available for Dedicated customers
